ask.text:
"How old are you, anyway?" (young) asks (subject) one morning, just making conversation.
It turns out nobody knows.
Not (subject). Not (subject.his/her) children. Not the oldest elders, who argue about it. Guesses range wildly, from "younger than me" to "older than the volcano." One person says (subject) was "already old when I was a baby", which (subject) finds deeply offensive.
(subject), meanwhile, seems to be enjoying the confusion enormously, and has started claiming a different age every time someone asks. (young) would like to give (subject) a proper birthday. But how does anyone celebrate a day nobody can remember?

text_only.reason: the word in the owner's story; what changes in the game is the ending's own EFFECT line (the ledger), so this word alone changes nothing

c1o1.text: (subject) decides at once, and very precisely, exactly how the day should go: a swim in the lagoon at sunrise, the biggest meal anyone can cook, and a very long nap in the best hammock in the village. Nobody else gets the hammock. The day goes exactly as planned, and (subject) declares it the best birthday (subject.he/she) has had in at least eighty years. Or sixty. Or a hundred.

c1o2.text: (subject) considers this, then asks for help planning a feast, a proper one, with drums. Everyone who thought (subject.he/she) hated fuss is astonished. The feast is loud, long and wonderful, and (subject) dances, badly and with great joy, until the moon is high.

c1.text: "Well," says (young), "if nobody knows your birthday, you might as well pick one. What would you like to do on it?"...

c2o1.text: (subject) teaches (young) how the old people counted years by the great events everyone remembered: the storm that knocked down the big palm, the year the comet came, the dry season when the stream vanished. (young) learns a useful way of reckoning time, and between them they work out that (subject) is somewhere between "quite old" and "very old." (subject) says that sounds about right.

text_only.reason: the word in the owner's story; what changes in the game is the ending's own EFFECT line (the ledger), so this word alone changes nothing

c2o2.text: They start counting storms, and then get stuck: (subject) can't remember which great storm came first, the one that took the fishing huts or the one that flooded the gardens. (subject.He/She) asks the other elders to help put the years in order, and soon the whole elders' circle is shouting about storms. They never settle it.

c2.text: (young) is determined to solve the mystery properly. (subject) chuckles. "If you want to count years, you don't count them. You count storms."...

c3o1.text: The evening passes in swapped memories, funny ones and sad ones and ones that make everyone groan. (subject) laughs until (subject.he/she) cries. By the end, nobody needs an exact number after all. "However old I am," (subject) says, "it's been worth it."

c3o2.text: An old disagreement comes up: whose idea was the first cooking hut? (subject) insists it was (subject.his/hers). Another elder insists it was theirs. It goes on for some time. Everyone agrees, eventually, to leave it unsettled, which is how both of them like it.

c3.text: That evening, (subject)'s family and friends gather around the fire to share memories of all the years they've known (subject.him/her)...
